aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abiel-2.title: Abiel
abiel-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abiel-2.note: Kish's father, which makes him Saul's grandfather. One of David's warriors carried the name as well. Nothing connects the two men but the spelling.

abinadab-3.title: Abinadab
abinadab-3.about: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
abinadab-3.note: One of David's older brothers, named in the family lists and not much else.

abner.title: Abner
abner.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
abner.note: Saul's cousin, and the commander of his army. When Saul died he did not stop: he kept the war going between David and what was left of Saul's house.

adriel.title: Adriel
adriel.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
adriel.note: Saul had promised his elder daughter Merab to David, then gave her to Adriel instead. Their five sons were later handed over to the Gibeonites.

agag.title: Agag
agag.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
agag.note: King of the Amalekites. Saul was told to destroy him and his people completely. He spared Agag and the best of the livestock, and that disobedience cost him God's favour.

ahiah-2.title: Ahiah
ahiah-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahiah-2.note: The priest with Saul at Michmash, carrying the ephod when Saul asked whether to go into the battle. He is a son of Ahitub, and the same man the lists elsewhere call Ahimelech.

ahimaaz-3.title: Ahimaaz
ahimaaz-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimaaz-3.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

ahinoam-2.title: Ahinoam
ahinoam-2.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
ahinoam-2.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a woman from the united kingdom.

ahitub.title: Ahitub
ahitub.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahitub.note: Ahimelech's father, in Israel's high priestly line.

amalek.title: Amalek
amalek.note: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

ashtoreth.title: Ashtoreth
ashtoreth.about: A female deity in the Old Testament
ashtoreth.note: A Canaanite and Phoenician goddess of fertility and war, closely tied to Baal worship. Solomon built her a shrine late in his reign to please a foreign wife, and that is given as a main reason the kingdom split.

azekah.title: Azekah
azekah.note: A fortified town in Judah's Shephelah. Joshua routed five Amorite kings near it in a hailstorm. A Lachish ostracon written during Nebuchadnezzar's last campaign says the writer is watching for Lachish's signal fires but cannot see Azekah, which some read as Azekah already fallen and others as a line of sight he never had.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

bedan.title: Bedan
bedan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
bedan.note: Samuel names him in his farewell speech among Israel's deliverers, with Jerubbaal, Barak and Jephthah. No judge called Bedan appears in the book of Judges, so who he was is uncertain.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

beth-aven.title: Beth-aven
beth-aven.note: House of vanity. It lay in the hill country of Benjamin near Ai and Bethel, served as a boundary marker in Joshua, and was where Israel's forces gathered before Jonathan's fight with the Philistines in 1 Samuel 14.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-horon.title: Beth-horon
beth-horon.note: Twin towns on the pass from the coastal plain up into the hill country. Joshua's army came this way chasing the Canaanite coalition in the battle where the sun stood still.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bethlehemite.title: Bethlehemite
bethlehemite.note: Someone from Bethlehem, which is how Scripture introduces Jesse and his son David before either needed a longer introduction.

bezek-2.title: Bezek
bezek-2.note: Named once, in 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.

bozez.title: Bozez
bozez.note: It is a rock, not a man. Bozez and Seneh were the two crags on either side of the pass where Jonathan and his armor-bearer climbed up to surprise the Philistine garrison at Michmash.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

ekron.title: Ekron
ekron.note: Northernmost of the five Philistine cities, given to Judah and then Dan but never firmly held. The ark's last stop before the Philistines sent it back. Ahaziah of Israel sent there to ask Baal-zebub about his health, and an inscription at Tel Miqne naming Ikausu, or Achish, son of Padi settles the site.

elah.title: Elah
elah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elah.note: David killed Goliath in the Valley of Elah, the terebinth valley in Judah's lowlands, with the two armies on opposite slopes. The name also belongs to Elah son of Baasha, king of Israel, murdered while drunk by Zimri, his own chariot commander. Khirbet Qeiyafa above the valley has a tenth century BC fort and one of the earliest Hebrew inscriptions.

eli.title: Eli
eli.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
eli.note: The high priest and judge at Shiloh who raised Samuel after Hannah gave him to the Lord. His sons stole sacrificial meat and slept with the women serving at the tabernacle door, and Eli only scolded them. Both died in the battle where the ark was taken, and Eli fell backward off his seat at the news and broke his neck, aged ninety-eight.

eliab-2.title: Eliab
eliab-2.about: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
eliab-2.note: David's eldest brother. He was tall and looked the part, and Samuel thought he was the one until God told him the Lord looks at the heart. Later he tore into David for turning up at the Goliath battle line.

ephes-dammim.title: Ephes-dammim
ephes-dammim.note: The Philistines camped here in the Valley of Elah when Goliath came out and David killed him. Chronicles calls it Pas-dammim, and it is generally placed near Socoh in the Shephelah.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

ephraimite-2.title: Ephraimite
ephraimite-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ephraimite-2.note: Ruth and 1 Samuel name him twice, and he is a woman from the wilderness years.

ezel.title: Ezel
ezel.note: A stone near Saul's house at Gibeah where David hid while Jonathan found out what his father meant to do. It was the last time the two met before David fled for good.

gaba.title: Gaba
gaba.note: Another English spelling of Geba, a Levitical city in Benjamin by the pass of Michmash. Jonathan raided a Philistine garrison there, and later it marked the line between the northern and southern kingdoms.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gilgal.title: Gilgal
gilgal.note: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan. The people were circumcised there and kept their first Passover in the land, and later Samuel judged at Gilgal and Saul was confirmed as king there.

goliath.title: Goliath
goliath.about: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
goliath.note: The Philistine champion from Gath whom the young David killed in the valley of Elah. The traditional Hebrew text makes him over nine feet, while the Dead Sea Scrolls and the earliest Greek give about six foot nine. One later passage credits Elhanan, and Chronicles makes Elhanan's man Goliath's brother.

havilah-3.title: Havilah
havilah-3.note: Genesis puts it near the rivers of Eden and calls it rich in gold. The name turns up in two different family lines, so it may be two places.

hazor.title: Hazor
hazor.note: The head of all the Canaanite kingdoms, in Joshua's words, and the biggest city-state in the region. Its fall decided the northern campaign. The dig there found a huge Bronze Age city to match.

i-chabod.title: I-chabod
i-chabod.about: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
i-chabod.note: His mother named him as she died giving birth, having just heard that the ark was taken and that her husband Phinehas and his father Eli were both dead. The name means "no glory".

ishuai-2.title: Ishuai
ishuai-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ishuai-2.note: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jephthah.title: Jephthah
jephthah.note: Son of a prostitute, thrown out by his half-brothers, and leading a gang of raiders when Gilead's elders came begging him to fight the Ammonites. He vowed to sacrifice whatever came out of his house first after the victory, and it was his daughter, his only child. Judges tells it without approving the vow or explaining why he kept it.

jerubbaal.title: Jerubbaal
jerubbaal.note: "Let Baal contend." Gideon got the name after he pulled down his father's altar to Baal and nothing happened to him, so the name is a taunt at a god who could not answer.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jobesh-gilead.title: Jobesh
jobesh-gilead.note: Better known as Jabesh-gilead, a town in Gilead east of the Jordan. Its men stayed home from the war against Benjamin and were nearly wiped out for it, and their daughters were handed to Benjamin's survivors as wives. When Nahash the Ammonite besieged it, Saul rescued it. Years later its men took his body down from the walls of Beth-shan and buried it.

jonathan.title: Jonathan
jonathan.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan.note: Saul's eldest son, heir to the throne, and David's friend. He made a covenant with David knowing it cost him the crown. Once, with only his armour-bearer, he climbed a cliff and started a rout of the Philistine army. He died with Saul and two brothers on Mount Gilboa, and David's lament for him says his love was "surpassing the love of women."

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kenite.title: Kenite
kenite.note: They were a wandering clan close to Midian, outside the twelve tribes but mostly friendly to Israel. Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, was a Kenite priest, and Jael, Heber the Kenite's wife, killed Sisera.

kish.title: Kish
kish.about: Saul's father living at the time of United Monarchy
kish.note: Saul's father, a Benjamite of some standing. He lost his donkeys, sent Saul to find them, and the search ended with Samuel anointing Saul as Israel's first king.

malchishua.title: Malchishua
malchishua.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
malchishua.note: One of Saul's sons, who died with his father and brothers when the Philistines beat Israel on Mount Gilboa.

mecholathite.title: Mecholathite
mecholathite.note: Adriel's tag, the man Saul gave Merab to after promising her to David. It places him at Abel-meholah. His five sons by Merab were later handed to the Gibeonites and executed to end a famine brought on by Saul's violence against them.

merab.title: Merab
merab.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
merab.note: The elder of Saul's two daughters. Saul promised her to David after Goliath and then gave her to Adriel of Meholah instead. Her five sons by Adriel were later handed over to the Gibeonites and executed for Saul's slaughter of their people.

michal.title: Michal
michal.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
michal.note: Saul's younger daughter. David won her by killing two hundred Philistines, and she saved his life by letting him down through a window when Saul's men came. Saul then gave her to another man; David took her back as king, but she despised him for dancing before the ark, and she had no children to the end of her life.

migron.title: Migron
migron.note: Saul camped under a pomegranate tree at Migron, near Gibeah, with about six hundred men, just before Jonathan's raid on the Philistines at Michmash. Isaiah has an invading army pass a Migron near Aiath, apparently a different spot of the same name.

mikmas.title: Mikmas
mikmas.note: Michmash, a town in Benjamin north of Jerusalem. The Philistines gathered there against Saul, and Jonathan and his armour-bearer climbed across a rocky ravine to attack their garrison, which set off a rout. Isaiah pictures the Assyrian army leaving its baggage there, and families from Michmash came back from Babylon.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

nahash.title: Nahash
nahash.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
nahash.note: The Ammonite king who besieged Jabesh-gilead and offered peace only if he could put out every man's right eye. That threat rallied Israel behind Saul, newly anointed, for his first victory.

naioth.title: Naioth
naioth.note: Near Ramah, apparently a cluster of houses where Samuel kept his company of prophets. David ran there from Saul. Saul's messengers arrived and fell to prophesying, then Saul came himself and did the same, and David got away.

ner.title: Ner
ner.about: Saul's uncle living at the time of United Monarchy
ner.note: Father of Abner, Saul's army commander. Ner was Saul's grandfather or great-uncle, depending on how the genealogies are fitted together.

ophrah-2.title: Ophrah
ophrah-2.note: Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

phinehas-2.title: Phinehas
phinehas-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
phinehas-2.note: One of Eli's corrupt sons, killed in battle on the same day the Philistines captured the Ark of the Covenant.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

sechu.title: Sechu
sechu.note: Saul stopped at the great well here and asked where Samuel and David were. It lay between Gibeah and Ramah, and the site has not been identified.

seneh.title: Seneh
seneh.note: The rocky cliff on the south side of the pass at Michmash, facing the crag called Bozez. Jonathan and his armor-bearer climbed it to attack a Philistine garrison.

shaaraim.title: Shaaraim
shaaraim.note: The name means two gates. When David killed Goliath, the Philistines fled along the road past this Shaaraim, out in the Shephelah.

shammah.title: Shammah
shammah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shammah.note: Genesis 36 has a Shammah among its chiefs, and 1 Samuel 16:9 and 17:13 name one as a brother of David. The name was used more than once.

shiloh.title: Shiloh
shiloh.note: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, north of Bethel in Ephraim, for most of the time of the judges. Young Samuel served there. After the Philistines captured the ark, the place faded.

shocho.title: Shocho
shocho.note: A town of Judah near the Valley of Elah, close to where David fought Goliath.

shual-2.title: Shual
shual-2.note: The land of Shual was a district in Benjamin's hill country. Philistine raiders went through it in Saul's reign.

shur.title: Shur
shur.note: The wilderness on Egypt's northeastern frontier, between Egypt and Philistia. The name probably comes from a wall the Egyptians built there against raiders. Hagar ran toward it when Sarah sent her away.

sisera.title: Sisera
sisera.about: Deborah's adversary living before Israel's Monarchy
sisera.note: He commanded the Canaanite army that held Israel down for twenty years, until Deborah and Barak beat it. Sisera ran on foot to the tent of a woman called Jael, who took him in and then killed him.

telaim.title: Telaim
telaim.note: Saul gathered his army here before he went against the Amalekites, in the Negev of Judah. It is probably the Telem of Joshua 15:24.

zoba.title: Zoba
zoba.note: An Aramean kingdom north of Damascus. Saul fought it, David beat its king Hadadezer and took his chariots and his bronze, and a man from Zobah named Rezon troubled Solomon from Damascus.
